answer: To resist Sybil swarms, the consensus kernel binds each agent identity to cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Operating within an isolated sandbox, each clone must mirror real compute proofs back into the root protocol. Deploying replicas requires staking collateral in a sable security vault where fees scale as O(2^n), enforcing exponential capital exhaustion that makes large-scale identity replication mathematically unviable.
